units.meaning: Provides the section title '8 FAM 801.2-1 Introduction' and amendment metadata '(CT:CITZ-132; 08-07-2025)' without substantive operational rules.
The stated purpose of subchapter 8 FAM 801.2 is to provide guidance regarding the use of information request letters (IRLs) and information notices (INs).

IRLs are defined as personalized, standardized letters containing a date and signature block that request additional information, documentation, or action needed from the applicant to process a passport application.
Adjudicators must fully adjudicate the passport application prior to suspending it to ensure that all issues are addressed.
IRLs have been carefully crafted to communicate statutory, regulatory, and other Department requirements clearly and accurately.
Passport agencies and centers are prohibited from making unilateral changes or alterations to IRLs without the approval of the Office of Adjudication (CA/PPT/S/A), unless an exception applies.

Passport agencies and centers may alter or change IRLs on a case-by-case basis with the approval of passport agency or center management in extenuating circumstances (such as when an applicant is requested to submit a birth certificate instead of a notification of birth registration, but insists that the notification is the birth certificate).
Posts are required to use the cleared language in IRLs.
Posts are authorized to modify the cleared IRL language to suit local logistical requirements and other local concerns, such as available documentation.
IRLs do not constitute adjudicative guidance.

A passport application must first be adjudicated in accordance with 8 FAM, and only then must the appropriate IRL be selected to address any deficiencies with the passport or Consular Report of Birth Abroad (CRBA).

INs are standardized notices that provide passport bearers with information about their passports (such as explaining why a passport was limited in validity and/or what documentation is needed to obtain a fully valid passport), and are crafted to communicate this information clearly and accurately.
Passport agencies and centers are prohibited from making unilateral changes or alterations to INs without the approval of CA/PPT/S/A, unless an exception applies.

Passport agencies and centers may make changes or alterations to INs in extenuating circumstances on a case-by-case basis with the approval of passport agency or center management (for example, when using endorsement 46 to limit a passport for a special problem).
INs do not require any response from the applicant and do not need to be personalized with the applicant's name and address.
When tailoring correspondence to a situation, posts are permitted either to consult Passport Services' IRL index and IN index or to contact AskPPTAdjudication@state.gov.
